question: What is the primary purpose of emergency contraception?

options.A: To treat common sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To cause an abortion of an established pregnancy
options.C: To provide long-term protection against conception
options.D: To prevent pregnancy after unprotected sex

explanation: Emergency contraception stops fertilization or implantation after unprotected intercourse rather than terminating an existing pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: Why should emergency contraception not replace regular family planning methods?

options.A: It causes permanent infertility with repeated use
options.B: It protects against sexually transmitted infections instead
options.C: It has lower overall effectiveness than regular methods
options.D: It is completely unsafe to take more than once a year

explanation: Regular contraceptives are designed for continuous protection and have higher efficacy rates than emergency options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: What factor most heavily influences the success of emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: The time of day the pill is swallowed
options.B: The body weight of the female client
options.C: The brand name of the hormonal product
options.D: The timing of administration after intercourse

explanation: Taking emergency pills as early as possible after unprotected sex drastically increases their effectiveness. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: A client presents after a condom burst during intercourse. Is this a valid indication for emergency contraception?

options.A: Yes, but only if she is currently breastfeeding an infant
options.B: Yes, because barrier method failure is a primary indication
options.C: No, she must wait for her next menstrual period to check
options.D: No, barrier methods cannot fail if put on correctly

explanation: Condom breakage is a common contraceptive mishap that qualifies a client for emergency contraception. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: What is the main biological action of emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: Delaying or preventing the release of an egg
options.B: Thickening the uterine lining to trap sperm
options.C: Causing immediate shedding of the endometrium
options.D: Destroying a fertilized egg inside the uterus

explanation: ECPs work by suppressing the luteinizing hormone surge to delay ovulation so fertilization cannot occur. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: Which ECP type can be taken up to five days after unprotected intercourse?
explanation: Ulipristal acetate remains effective for up to 120 hours, which is five days post-intercourse. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: Within how many hours must a copper IUD be inserted for emergency contraception?
explanation: The copper IUD must be inserted within five days or 120 hours of unprotected intercourse to act as emergency contraception. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: What is a major dual benefit of choosing a copper IUD for emergency contraception?

options.A: It induces an instant abortion if implantation already occurred
options.B: It protects against HIV and other sexually transmitted infections
options.C: It completely stops menstrual bleeding and cramping pain
options.D: It provides immediate emergency action and long-term birth control

explanation: The IUD serves as emergency contraception and can stay in the uterus to prevent future pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: What crucial date must the nurse calculate during the client assessment?

options.A: Date of the last menstrual period
options.C: Date of the first sexual encounter
options.D: Date of the next expected vacation

explanation: Knowing the last menstrual period helps determine cycle day and rule out an existing pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: A client requests emergency pills 96 hours after unprotected sex. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Administer standard levonorgestrel and send her home immediately
options.B: Tell her that emergency contraception is no longer effective at all
options.C: Refuse treatment because levonorgestrel only works for 48 hours
options.D: Discuss ulipristal acetate or a copper IUD as viable options

explanation: Levonorgestrel window has passed at 96 hours, but ulipristal acetate and copper IUD remain effective up to 120 hours. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: Which common side effect often follows the ingestion of emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: Sudden high fever and skin rash
options.B: Severe chronic joint and muscle pain

explanation: Hormone surges frequently cause mild nausea and alter the timing of the upcoming menstrual period. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: Why is a confirmed pregnancy an absolute contraindication for emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: The pills are ineffective and will not terminate the pregnancy
options.B: The hormones will cause immediate birth defects in the fetus
options.C: The client will experience severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: The pregnant uterus rejects hormonal pills mechanically

explanation: Emergency contraceptives work before implantation and do not harm an established pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: A client fears emergency pills will cause permanent infertility. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Explain scientifically that EC has no permanent effect on future fertility
options.B: Prescribe traditional herbs instead to protect her reproductive system
options.C: Ignore her concern because it is an unimportant personal opinion
options.D: Confirm her fear and advise her never to use hormonal products again

explanation: Nurses must correct false beliefs by explaining that emergency contraception does not impair future ability to conceive. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: Which attitude is most important for a Nigerian nurse providing emergency contraception counseling?

options.C: Refusal of service based on personal beliefs

explanation: Creating a safe, welcoming environment encourages clients to seek timely care without fear of stigma. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)
